proposals.evidence: Turner 2462 §2 explicitly lists European Romani yek 'one' under *ēkka-. The source prints Zargari jekh [jek] 'one' (p. 127 §2.3.5) and explains that final aspirates may deaspirate. The same lemma recurs in the source numeral paradigm (p. 137 §3.5.1). Its separately imported yek spelling already has a rank-1 variant edge to this jekh record; that existing variant is not duplicated. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 9804 explicitly lists German/Hungarian/Welsh Romani maškər/maškár/maskal 'in, between' under mádhya. The source prints Zargari mośgār 'in the middle' among adverbs of place (p. 143 §3.20.1.3). Source §2.3.1 (p. 127) documents merger of voiceless nonaspirates with voiced consonants; the k/g difference is therefore source-compatible, while the vowel details are retained without a new sound-rule claim. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
